newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air seeks scrutiny on new AMR pact.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air seeks scrutiny on new AMR pact.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Friday it will ask the U.S. Department of Transportation to closely scrutinize the proposed alliance of American Airlines and British Airways in light of their pending marketing relationship with Spanish carrier Iberia.
Earlier on Friday, American and BA announced separate deals to link up with Iberia and tap into the Spanish carrier's southern European and Latin American markets.
American said it has a full marketing alliance with Iberia and is also buying a 10 percent stake in the parent of Iberia's associated Argentinian airlines Aerolineas Argentinas and Austral.

Meanwhile, BA will negotiate a marketing deal with Iberia and also to discuss the possibility of taking a minority stake in the Spanish state-owned carrier. Both American and BA have options to buy minority stakes in Iberia by the end of this year.

Continental said it will ask regulators to require the carriers involved to provide additional information on the Aerolineas Argentinas and Iberia investments so the effects in the markets can be examined in the context of the ongoing examination of the American-BA deal.

"This proposed alliance is another example of American and British Airways joining forces to crush competition and require the traveling public to pay the price," said Jeff Smisek, Executive Vice President and General Counsel of Continental Airlines.

"By combining dominance in the trans-Atlantic market with dominance in the Latin American market, American will strengthen its dominance in both markets, force competitors to withdraw, and preclude future competition," Smisek said.
Continental, which serves 19 countries and 32 markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, had previously been in talks for a deal with Aerolineas and Iberia.

"An investment in Aerolineas would have expedited our entrance into Argentina, but it is very likely that there will be open skies deal with Argentina in any event, so we may still be able to serve that market at some point," a Continental spokeswoman said.
